newsitem.title: USA: Miami judge lets second-hand smoke lawsuit proceed.
newsitem.headline: Miami judge lets second-hand smoke lawsuit proceed.

text.p: A Florida judge refused on Monday to decertify class action status in a second-hand smoke lawsuit brought by airline flight attendants against the tobacco industry.

Judge Robert Kaye also refused the tobacco companies' motion to deny the flight attendants' request for punitive damages in the class-action lawsuit known as Broin v Philip Morris et al. Kaye ruled on Friday but the rulings were sealed until Monday. Jury selection in the case was to begin Monday morning.
In other rulings, Kaye dismissed two of the defendants in the case, leaving nine defendants.

Dropped as defendants were Dosal Tobacco Co., a small family-owned cigarette maker in Opa-locka, Fla., and United States Tobacco Co., a unit of UST Co. Inc. and the largest seller of snuff and chewing tobacco.
Neither companies' products had been linked to any plaintiff in the case.
The suit contends that some 60,000 flight attendants contracted a variety of ailments, including lung cancer, from breathing other people's cigarette smoke on passenger jets.
